summary.en-US: See Strava's global heatmap and your personal heatmap on Mapy.com, for road, MTB, gravel, running or trail running. Plan a route, send it to Strava, and it syncs to your Garmin or Wahoo from there.

description.en-US:
Plan routes on Mapy.com with Strava's heat on top of the map.

- **Global heatmap by sport**: switch between Road, MTB, Gravel, Run and Trail Run.
- **Your personal heatmap** in blue on top of the global heat. Each layer turns on and off on its own, so the roads and trails you haven't done yet stand out.
- **Follows the map live**: the heat moves with every pan, zoom and rotation.
- **Sync to Strava**: save your planned Mapy.com route to your Strava account in one click, as a private, starred route. From there it syncs to your Garmin or Wahoo. Or download a plain GPX file (no account needed).
- **On-map panel** with opacity, a minimize button and keyboard shortcuts (A all, S sport, D global, F personal), plus fast tile caching.

You need to be logged in to Strava in Firefox. A Strava subscription is needed for the global heatmap above zoom 11, your personal heatmap and Sync to Strava. Route planning and the plain GPX download work on a free account.

Firefox asks for access to strava.com when you install. If you turn that off later, click the Heatmapy toolbar icon and use Grant access, because the heatmap can't load without it.

The extension only talks to Strava, using your existing login, and keeps its settings on your computer. Nothing is sent to the developer or anyone else.

An independent project, not affiliated with Strava or Mapy.com. Source code and issues: https://github.com/matejcermak/heatmapy

version.approval_notes:
Heatmapy overlays Strava heatmap tiles on mapy.com / mapy.cz and can save the route the user planned on Mapy.com to the user's own Strava account. No bundler or minifier: the uploaded files are the source (https://github.com/matejcermak/heatmapy, built by scripts/build.mjs, which only copies files and writes the Firefox manifest).

webRequest + webRequestBlocking: Firefox does not attach SameSite cookies to requests made by the extension's background page (the initiator is the moz-extension:// origin, so the request is cross-site), and a user logged in inside a container has their Strava session in a non-default cookie store that background fetch() cannot use. Every credentialed request to Strava therefore fails with 403 or a redirect to /login. background.js registers one blocking onBeforeSendHeaders listener, filtered to *://*.strava.com/*, that adds the user's own Strava cookies (read with the cookies API from the store that holds the Strava session) only to the extension's own requests (tabId === -1 and a moz-extension:// originUrl). It never touches page requests and never reads or changes any other site. Cookie is a forbidden header for fetch(), so this is the only way.

Network traffic: only to *.strava.com: heatmap tiles, athlete-ID detection, and (only when the user clicks Sync to Strava) creating a private route in the user's own Strava account. Nothing goes to the developer or any other third party; no analytics.

mapy-hook.js runs in the MAIN world on mapy.com / mapy.cz only. It reads the live map camera from Mapy's own map engine so the overlay can follow pans and zooms, and it captures the URL of Mapy's own GPX export when the user syncs a route. It passes data to the content script as a JSON string in a CustomEvent and via window.postMessage.

The 4 UNSAFE_VAR_ASSIGNMENT lint warnings in content.js are innerHTML assignments built only from extension string constants (panel markup, login banner, hint text, restoring the button's own markup). No page or user data is interpolated.

Testing: install, open https://mapy.com. Without a Strava login the on-map panel appears with a banner asking you to log in to Strava. With a free Strava account logged in, the global heatmap shows at zoom 11 and below. A Strava subscription is needed for higher zooms, the personal heatmap and Sync to Strava.
